text:
[{"rune": "Hagalaz", "text": "Underground, below the broken branches, the roots hold a shape the storm never reached. Hagalaz is the hail that strips a house down to what was built well. What stood before you was planted by hands you may never have seen, and what stands after will be rooted in soil you turn now. Kuky, some of what your family holds may be falling this season, and some of it may be the part that cannot."}]
✦ What in your house has survived weather before — and would you know it by looking?

[{"rune": "Hagalaz", "text": "Beneath the ground, the roots are holding, though no one standing in the wind can see them. The branches came off, the shape of the tree changed, and the tree is still there. This is Hagalaz — the storm takes what it can take, and what it cannot take stays. In a house of many generations, Kuky, this may be a thing lost that will not return, or a thing older than the storm that outlasts it.\n✦ Nothing here is owed or earned. What would you notice if you looked at what stayed, rather than what went?"}]

[{"rune": "Hagalaz", "text": "Under the soil, far below the broken branches, the roots hold their grip on stone. Hagalaz is the hail that strips a thing down to what was anchored all along. A house stands on what was buried by hands you never watched work. Kuky, this may be a roof that outlasts the ones who raised it, or a lineage that keeps only what was rooted deep.\n✦ Not everything falls. What has old roots in your house may be worth noticing before the weather asks."}]

[{"rune": "Hagalaz", "text": "Underground, where no eye reaches, the roots hold while the storm takes the branches. Hagalaz is the hail that strips a thing down to what was built to last. A house stands or falls the same way, through what was laid before anyone now living arrived. Kuky, some of what links you to your people may be falling, and some may be rooted too deep to move.\n✦ When the loud things have gone quiet, what is still standing — and how long had it been there before you noticed it?"}]

[{"rune": "Fehu", "text": "At the fence line the mountain gives way to pasture, and the sheep come down counted larger than they went up. Fehu is the flock that grew while it was out of sight, wealth that increases by being let loose rather than held. What was given in spring returns in autumn wearing a different shape. Between you and another, this may be a season of receiving, or a season where what you tend is still out grazing."}]

✦ What you keep feeding keeps growing — is there something in your hands now that has gone untended long enough to notice?

[{"rune": "Fehu", "text": "Where the home field ends and the mountain begins, the sheep come down, and the flock is bigger than the one that went up in spring. Fehu is that count at the gate, wealth that grew because it was let out and brought back. Nothing here was hoarded through the summer. What you hold may be increase waiting to be let loose, or warmth already returning to you from somewhere you had stopped counting."}]

✦ What sits untouched loses its strength — is there something in your keeping that would be more alive moving than held?

[{"rune": "Fehu", "text": "At the gate where the mountain path becomes home pasture, the flock comes down fuller than it went up. The lambs were not counted in spring, and now they crowd the fold. Fehu is wealth that only grew because it was kept moving and kept fed. What you hold between you may be richer than counted, or waiting on what you still have to give.\n✦ What you tend keeps growing; what is left standing goes quiet. Which of these is nearer to what rests in your hands now?"}]

[{"rune": "Fehu", "text": "Where the mountain pasture ends, the flock comes down into the home field, and the count is higher than when they went up. Fehu is wealth that lives and breeds, worth only what it is given room to do. Something held close all summer is counted now. What you give may be the increase, and what you receive may be the room it was given.\n✦ Fehu guarantees nothing. What comes in can go out again. What have you been keeping still that might grow if it moved?"}]

[{"rune": "Wunjo", "text": "At the edge of the bench, where the stranger's place turns into yours, someone shifts over and the question of why you came is never asked. Wunjo is ease that arrives without being earned. The friction is that no one hands you proof you belong, and you must sit there anyway, unverified. Kuky, something in you may be learning to stay seated without checking the door.\n✦ Wunjo asks: can you tell when your hands have already stopped gripping?"}]

[{"rune": "Wunjo", "text": "At the edge of the room the talk thins out, and the bench takes your weight without question. No one asks why you came; the door simply stood open and you walked through. Wunjo is that plain ease, a place where you are not explaining yourself. Yet the harder thing is staying seated, Kuky, and whether enough good has gathered here that you might rest in it."}]

✦ Where has something quietly fallen into place while you weren't watching — and could you loosen your hold on it for a moment?

[{"rune": "Wunjo", "text": "At the door the cold ends and the room begins, and you step through without explaining yourself. The bench holds you, nobody asks what you came for. Wunjo is that ease, the plain good of being counted among others. The hardest part is staying seated when nothing is demanded of you, Kuky — and it may be that this sitting still is itself the slow change.\n✦ When something fits without effort, do you notice it, or only the next thing that needs fixing?"}]

[{"rune": "Wunjo", "text": "At the door the cold air ends and the warm begins, and you cross without being asked why you came. Wunjo is that threshold — the ease of being counted in. The friction is that no one here will hand you the welcome; you have to sit down. Kuky, you may already be easier in company than you were.\n✦ When something fits without effort, do you notice it, or only look for what is still missing?"}]

[{"rune":"Hagalaz","text":"Below the tree before you, roots grip soil beyond the reach of the storm. You see a split branch hanging above the ground, but the trunk still stands. Hagalaz names change that leaves some things standing. Kuky, your link to generations before and after may be a lasting bond or a broken one.\n✦ Does change in your life always mean that everything is lost?"}]

[{"rune":"Hagalaz","text":"Below the ground at your feet, the roots of one standing tree remain hidden after the storm. Hagalaz names the change that leaves some things standing and others broken. Across your family's generations, the same question remains, Kuky. What links you to those before and after may be a lasting bond or a lasting break.\n✦ Can you look at what changes without calling it punishment?"}]

[{"rune":"Hagalaz","text":"Out of your sight, the roots hold beneath the tree left standing after the storm. Above them, a split branch hangs over the ground. Hagalaz names change that breaks some things without breaking everything. Kuky, your link to those before and after you may be a bond still holding, or one coming apart.\n✦ Can you name a change without calling it punishment?"}]

[{"rune":"Hagalaz","text":"Under your feet, the surviving tree’s roots hold soil where the storm strips it bare. You see a split branch hanging above the doorway. Hagalaz names change that leaves some things standing. Kuky, your link to those before and after you may be a lasting shelter, or a break that remains open.\n✦ Can you name change without calling it punishment or assuming everything must fall?"}]

[{"rune":"Fehu","text":"At your gate, mountain grazing becomes winter keeping as the sheep press through. You count more backs than in spring, with burrs caught in their wool. Fehu names wealth that needs care, rather than possession alone. What you give may be care that sustains, and what you receive may be care returned.\n✦ What in your keeping remains strong through use?"}]

[{"rune":"Fehu","text":"At your gate, the mountain track meets earth worn bare by returning hooves. You count more sheep than in spring, with lambs pressing against their mothers. Fehu names wealth you can nourish rather than merely possess. What you give may be nourishment, and what you receive may be enough to nourish another.\n✦ What remains yours through tending, rather than through keeping?"}]

[{"rune":"Fehu","text":"At your gate, the sheep come down from the mountain, wool catching on rough wood. You count more than in spring, with smaller hooves crowding beside the ewes. Fehu names the living wealth you see, dependent on care. What you give may be care that multiplies, or what you receive may be care returned.\n✦ What in your keeping needs care rather than merely possession?"}]

[{"rune":"Fehu","text":"At your gate, the mountain flock becomes a household's wealth, with more sheep than in spring. You hear their hooves knock against the wooden threshold. Fehu names wealth that needs care and can pass between hands. What you give may be care that keeps affection alive, while what you receive may be care returned.\n✦ What in your care needs more than possession to keep its value?"}]

[{"rune":"Wunjo","text":"You cross from standing apart to sitting among them, your chair scraping the floor. Wunjo names belonging without having to explain your presence. No one asks why you came, but you still have to occupy the seat. Kuky, your slow change may be enjoying what is good without first making yourself useful.\n✦ Does something have to count as a victory before you can enjoy it?"}]

[{"rune":"Wunjo","text":"You pass from standing apart to sitting with them, and no one asks why you came. Your chair scrapes the floor, but the conversation continues without an explanation from you. With Wunjo, you have a place without having to justify it. Kuky, you may slowly be enjoying company without treating welcome as a debt.\n✦ Can you enjoy what fits without needing it to be a victory?"}]

[{"rune":"Wunjo","text":"You pass from standing beside the table to sitting with them, and no one asks why you came. Wunjo names belonging that asks you for no explanation. You have a seat, not a promise that every silence is easy. Kuky, you may be growing less quick to turn a good moment into a test.\n✦ Can you enjoy what fits without asking it to last?"}]

[{"rune":"Wunjo","text":"You cross from the doorway into their conversation, and your chair scrapes without drawing a question. With Wunjo, you have a place that needs no explanation. You sit among them, but being included is not the same as enjoying it. Kuky, you may slowly become less occupied with earning what is already offered.\n✦ Can something be good without you having to secure it against every possible loss?"}]
